findings.title: A mouse move over the grid takes the new snapshot before refresh() checks it, so a selection can stay on lines that slid away at the top of a full scrollback
findings.evidence: refresh_holds_view (terminal.rs:382-391) compares the new snapshot with self.grid, the last snapshot taken. handle_mouse calls tab.refresh() (terminal.rs:1218) for every event in the grid area. That includes MK::Moved, which crossterm's EnableMouseCapture (main.rs:61, any-event tracking) reports on every mouse move. Scenario: the scrollback is full, the user scrolls the view to its very top (scroll_offset == scrollback_len) and selects text, output keeps streaming, and the mouse moves over the grid. The hover snapshot already shows the slid screen, with the offset unchanged at the cap. Then refresh() sees old == new cells, the check (g.scroll_offset < g.scrollback_len || g.cells == old.cells) passes, and the selection is kept, highlighting text it never covered. Only the highlight is wrong: copy_selection ran on release, so the clipboard is correct. Only this cap-top case is affected; below the cap the emulator keeps the view on its lines.
findings.fix_suggestion: Make the hold decision against the snapshot from when the selection was made or last held, not against whichever snapshot was taken last. For example, store the (scroll_offset, cells hash or scrollback_len) seen at the last refresh() or selection on the panel and compare against that. Or skip tab.refresh() in handle_mouse for MK::Moved when the program does not report the mouse. Add a test: a full scrollback viewed at its top with a selection, a mouse move over the grid between the output and the wake, then expect the selection to be dropped.
